items.title: Injectivity of a homomorphism of finite modules over a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring from the determinant at the prime, with the length of the cokernel given by an order
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the chapter's Key Lemma. Under the hypothesis that M and N each admit generating sequences x_1,...,x_l and y_1,...,y_l whose successive quotients are all isomorphic to R/q with dim(R/q) = 1, it asserts that phi : M -> N is injective if and only if phi_q is an isomorphism, and that then length_R(Coker(phi)) equals the order ord_{R/q}(f) of the residue-field element f defined by [phi(x_1),...,phi(x_l)] = f [y_1,...,y_l] in det_{kappa(q)}(N_q) (statement lines 17803-17828). The proof is a genuine double induction: the case l = 1 and the diagonal case phi(x_i) = f_i y_i with f_i not in q are disposed of first (proof lines 17831-17858); then for general l one lets i be minimal with phi(x_1) in <y_1,...,y_i>, rescales the x_j and y_j by a to reach a = 1 and computes length_R(M/M') = (l-1) ord(a) together with length_R(N/N') = (l-i+1) ord(a) to obtain length_R(Coker(phi')) = length_R(Coker(phi)) + i ord(a) while f' = a^i f, and finally uses the admissible relations of the determinant to replace y_1,...,y_l by the transposed sequence, which decreases the invariant i by one (proof lines 17861-17956). The coordination of the determinant condition with the length bookkeeping under a change of generating sequences is the crux of the argument and is not a routine exercise, so the claim is H3.
